findings.title: No-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not exist
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments so re-authentication will not skip the username form when passkeys are on. The only new method is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), and UsernameForm does not define a no-arg overload. This does not compile, so the username-form flow (and PasskeysUsernameFormTest) cannot be built. The call needs a real method: either pass context.getUser(), or add a no-arg helper that only checks that the passkeys feature and realm policy are enabled.

findings.title: Conditional passkey UI dropped when user is unknown
findings.body: authenticate() and the error challenge() (line 137) now call fillContextForm only when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true. That helper (line 161) requires a non-null user, replacing the previous checks that set up WebAuthn conditional UI precisely when the user was not yet selected (webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled(), and user == null on errors). Moving the call outside the else does not restore the anonymous case. On a normal login the user is null, so the page never gets the WebAuthn challenge, rpId, or ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI. Discoverable-credential auto-login, the webauth form, and "username webauthn" autocomplete fail on the initial page and on invalid-username/invalid-password redisplay. Only re-authentication, where a user is already on the context, still sets up passkeys. Passkeys should be filled whenever the feature is enabled, whether or not a user is already known.
